headline: Variant class-toggles fold to a string concat, so `next-yak-9.7` and `next-yak-css-9.7` render each card with no hash-and-inject and sit at the static-class floor, while the runtime libraries pay `generateAndInjectStyles`/`murmur2` per card.

microbench.why: The `$discount`/`$wishlisted` variants compile to class toggles, so `next-yak-9.7` inlines them to a string concat and never hashes or injects — its library slice is 0.316 ms of a 2.43 ms render. `vanilla` (0.317 ms/1k) and the css-prop fold (`next-yak-css-9.7`, 0.324 ms/1k) share that same static-class floor. Of the field that stays slow, the hash-and-inject runtimes dominate: `styled-components` re-runs `generateAndInjectStyles` per card (library slice 3.34 ms), `goober` re-serializes and hashes (3.34 ms), and `emotion`'s standalone `murmur2` pushes its slice to 7.14 ms — 3.6× to 7× off the folded lanes.

autocannon.why: Under a real server loop the ranking follows render cost: the folded yak lanes and `vanilla` clear ~285 req/s because each request re-renders static classes, while `emotion` (75.0 req/s) and `panda` (110 req/s) re-run their per-card serializers on every request. The css-prop and styled folds land within noise of `vanilla`; the runtime libraries never recover the parse-hash-inject time they spend per request.

attribution.why: The whole SSR split is the library slice: `vanilla` and the atomic/extracted lanes carry ~0 lib ms (`stylex` 0.048, `next-yak-css-9.7` 0.164, `next-yak-9.7` 0.316 after the toggle fold), so their render time is almost pure react-dom. What separates the pack is what each still computes per card — `styled-components` spends 3.34 ms of its 6.40 ms render in `generateAndInjectStyles`, and `emotion` 7.14 ms of 13.0 ms in serialize-plus-`murmur2`. Disabling folding shows the lever directly: `next-yak-9.7-nofold` lib jumps to 1.07 ms (render 3.88 ms) because the `Yak` wrapper renders per card instead of vanishing.

hydrate.why: Extracted lanes ship the sheet in the HTML, so hydration is pure JS with zero style/layout/paint — `panda`, `next-yak-css-9.7`, `vanilla` and `next-yak-9.7` cluster at 55-59 ms within their spread. The runtime libraries inject their stylesheet on the client while hydrating: `styled-components` burns 5.75 ms in layout and `goober` 5.45 ms recalculating once the sheet lands, dragging them to 250 ms and 237 ms — 4.3× the extracted floor. The top of the cluster is a statistical tie; the mechanism split (static sheet vs client injection) is the certain result.

inp.why: The whole static-class cluster (`vanilla`, `cnfast`, `stylex`, `next-yak-css-9.7`, `next-yak-9.7`) sits at 8-9 ms of interaction work — inside the ~20% run-to-run spread this measurement carries, so their order is noise. The signal is the gap to the runtime libraries: `styled-components` 28.8 ms, `goober` 31.3 ms and `emotion` 46.5 ms re-enter their serialize-and-inject path when the interaction re-renders, tripling to quintupling the interaction cost.

mount.why: Cold mount adds first-paint styling cost to the render. Extracted lanes mount at ~125-131 ms because the browser parses one static sheet once; the runtime libraries pay their first hash-and-inject on top of mount — `goober` 201 ms, `styled-components` 211 ms, `emotion` 228 ms. The extracted lanes differ only within their ~1.5% spread, so the css-prop lead over `vanilla` is a tie; the runtime penalty is the real result.

renderTiming.why: Every lane triggers exactly one Chrome style recalc for the batch, extracted and runtime alike — none causes extra layout thrash, so the count is a flat parity. The sub-millisecond styleMs spread (0.233-0.725 ms) does not track the styling method and sits inside measurement noise.

payload.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` folds each element's variants into a single className (7.20 kB gz), just under `vanilla`; the styled fold ships one hashed class per element (8.30 kB). The utility lanes carry every atomic token in the markup — `cnfast` 27.6 kB, `tailwind-merge` 26.6 kB, 3.3× — and the runtime libraries add their client bundle plus rules (`styled-components` 21.2 kB, `panda` 21.1 kB, `emotion` 20.2 kB).

nsweep.why: As the grid grows to 4000 cards the per-element cost compounds: the folded css-prop lane and `vanilla` scale flat with react-dom (~18 ms), the styled fold trails slightly at 21.0 ms, and the hash libraries diverge — `goober` 67.3 ms, `styled-components` 69.2 ms, `emotion` 131 ms — because each new card re-pays its serialize-hash-inject.

crossCase: `product-grid` is the case where next-yak's fold applies: its variants are class toggles (`$discount`, `$wishlisted`), which inline to string concats. Contrast `dyn-translate` shown alongside, whose per-element numeric value compiles to a CSS variable and keeps the runtime wrapper — the fold triggers on toggles, not on dynamic values.
